paragraphs.source_en: You gentlemen probably know what a square-lattice fence is. It is a wall that lets the wind pass through and is extremely easy to put up. As for me, I can pass in and out freely through the openings, so whether the fence is built or not makes no difference to me. But the headmaster of Rakunkan did not build the square-lattice fence for the sake of this cat; he deliberately brought in workmen to put it up so that the gentlemen he was cultivating would not be able to crawl out. True, however well it may be ventilated, a human being does not seem able to crawl through it. To pass through one of these four-inch-square holes woven out of bamboo would probably be difficult even for Zhang Shizun himself, the Chinese magician. Therefore, for human beings, this wall undoubtedly performs fully the function of a wall. It is no wonder that my master was delighted when he saw it completed and thought, “This should do nicely.” However, there was a great hole in my master’s logic, a hole larger than those in the bamboo fence, a vast hole through which even a fish big enough to swallow a boat might escape. For my master began from the assumption that a wall is not something to be climbed over; he assumed that, since they were students of a school, however crude the wall might be, so long as there was something bearing the name of a wall and the boundary was clearly marked, there was no fear that they would invade again. And even if he set that assumption aside, he still concluded that, should anyone try to break in, they could not possibly do so. For he hastily decided that no boy, however small and thin, could ever crawl through the openings of such a lattice fence, and that therefore there was no need to fear another intrusion. And indeed, so long as they are not cats, there is no likelihood that they will pass through those square openings. Even if they wanted to, they absolutely could not. But climbing over it and jumping across it is the simplest thing in the world; if anything, it makes good exercise.

units.source_en: You gentlemen probably know what a square-lattice fence is.
units.source_zh: 诸位大概了解方格篱笆是怎么回事吧。

units.source_en: It is a wall that lets the wind pass through and is extremely easy to put up.
units.source_zh: 它是一种既便于通风、筑起来又非常简便的墙。

units.source_en: As for me, I can pass in and out freely through the openings, so whether the fence is built or not makes no difference to me.

ja.t: る。こしらえたって、こしらえなくたって

units.source_zh: 像我就可以从格子眼中自由自在地出入，所以筑不筑篱笆，对于我是一样的。

units.source_en: But the headmaster of Rakunkan did not build the square-lattice fence for the sake of this cat; he deliberately brought in workmen to put it up so that the gentlemen he was cultivating would not be able to crawl out.

ja.t: られんために、わざわざ

units.source_zh: 然而落云馆校长可不是为我这只猫筑的方格篱笆，而是为了不让他自己培养的这群君子钻出去才特地请来工匠筑上的。

units.source_en: True, however well it may be ventilated, a human being does not seem able to crawl through it.
units.source_zh: 不错，不管筑得如何有利于通风，人毕竟是无法钻过去的。

units.source_en: To pass through one of these four-inch-square holes woven out of bamboo would probably be difficult even for Zhang Shizun himself, the Chinese magician.

ja.t: といえどもむずかしい。

units.source_zh: 人想要从这个用竹子编成的、四寸见方的窟窿钻过去，即使请来中国的魔术师张世尊，恐怕也是件大难事。

units.source_en: Therefore, for human beings, this wall undoubtedly performs fully the function of a wall.
units.source_zh: 所以这堵墙对人来说，无疑是起到了墙的作用。

units.source_en: It is no wonder that my master was delighted when he saw it completed and thought, “This should do nicely.”

ja.t: て、これならよかろうと

units.source_zh: 难怪主人看到这堵墙修好，认为“这下可好了”，十分高兴。

units.source_en: However, there was a great hole in my master’s logic, a hole larger than those in the bamboo fence, a vast hole through which even a fish big enough to swallow a boat might escape.
units.source_zh: 但是，主人的逻辑中却有个极大的漏洞，这个漏洞比这堵竹墙上的窟窿还要大，是个足以使吞舟之鱼都会漏网的极大的漏洞。

units.source_en: For my master began from the assumption that a wall is not something to be climbed over; he assumed that, since they were students of a school, however crude the wall might be, so long as there was something bearing the name of a wall and the boundary was clearly marked, there was no fear that they would invade again.

ja.t: ゆべきものにあらずとの

units.source_zh: 因为主人从墙是不可逾越的这一假定出发的，是建立在既然是学校的学生，不管这墙建造得如何粗糙，只要有个名叫墙的东西，明确了区域的界限，就不必担心他们会再闯进来的假定之上的。

units.source_en: And even if he set that assumption aside, he still concluded that, should anyone try to break in, they could not possibly do so.
units.source_zh: 而且即使他推翻这个假定，他也认为，纵然有人想要闯进来也是闯不进的。

units.source_en: For he hastily decided that no boy, however small and thin, could ever crawl through the openings of such a lattice fence, and that therefore there was no need to fear another intrusion.

ja.t: してしまったのである。

units.source_zh: 因为他轻率地断定，任何瘦小的少年也绝不可能钻过这种方格窟窿，从而不必担心会有人再闯进来。

units.source_en: And indeed, so long as they are not cats, there is no likelihood that they will pass through those square openings.
units.source_zh: 事实也的确如此，只要他们不是猫儿，就不会出现从这种四方窟窿钻过来的可能。

units.source_en: Even if they wanted to, they absolutely could not.
units.source_zh: 他们就是想做也绝对办不到。

units.source_en: But climbing over it and jumping across it is the simplest thing in the world; if anything, it makes good exercise.
units.source_zh: 不过，跳过来蹦过去，却是极简单的啊，反而可以成为运动嘛。

paragraphs.source_zh: 诸位大概了解方格篱笆是怎么回事吧。它是一种既便于通风、筑起来又非常简便的墙。像我就可以从格子眼中自由自在地出入，所以筑不筑篱笆，对于我是一样的。然而落云馆校长可不是为我这只猫筑的方格篱笆，而是为了不让他自己培养的这群君子钻出去才特地请来工匠筑上的。不错，不管筑得如何有利于通风，人毕竟是无法钻过去的。人想要从这个用竹子编成的、四寸见方的窟窿钻过去，即使请来中国的魔术师张世尊，恐怕也是件大难事。所以这堵墙对人来说，无疑是起到了墙的作用。难怪主人看到这堵墙修好，认为“这下可好了”，十分高兴。但是，主人的逻辑中却有个极大的漏洞，这个漏洞比这堵竹墙上的窟窿还要大，是个足以使吞舟之鱼都会漏网的极大的漏洞。因为主人从墙是不可逾越的这一假定出发的，是建立在既然是学校的学生，不管这墙建造得如何粗糙，只要有个名叫墙的东西，明确了区域的界限，就不必担心他们会再闯进来的假定之上的。而且即使他推翻这个假定，他也认为，纵然有人想要闯进来也是闯不进的。因为他轻率地断定，任何瘦小的少年也绝不可能钻过这种方格窟窿，从而不必担心会有人再闯进来。事实也的确如此，只要他们不是猫儿，就不会出现从这种四方窟窿钻过来的可能。他们就是想做也绝对办不到。不过，跳过来蹦过去，却是极简单的啊，反而可以成为运动嘛。
